projects.title: Weapon Detection with Vision-Language Model Validation for Intelligent Surveillance
projects.description:
Undergraduate thesis research focused on improving weapon detection reliability by integrating object detection models with Vision-Language Models (VLMs). The proposed framework employs a two-stage pipeline where a detector identifies potential weapons, and a VLM performs contextual validation and reasoning to verify detections, reducing false positives and enhancing explainability.

The study investigates how multimodal AI can strengthen conventional computer vision systems by incorporating semantic understanding and visual reasoning, making weapon detection more robust for real-world surveillance and public safety applications.

projects.title: Eye Blink to Morse Code Decoder
projects.description: I served as the Project Leader for Eye Blink Decoder, a computer vision–based system that translates eye blinks into Morse code for hands-free communication using a standard webcam. The project utilizes MediaPipe FaceMesh to extract facial landmarks and compute the Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR) for real-time blink detection, where blink duration is classified into short and long signals and decoded into readable text. My role involved designing the system architecture, leading the algorithm and model selection process, integrating computer vision and decoding logic, and coordinating development and testing to ensure real-time performance and robustness under varying conditions. This project highlights the application of computer vision and human–computer interaction techniques in building assistive communication technologies.

projects.title: Performance Evaluation of YOLOv12 Variants for Trash Detection in Mountain Hiking Trail Environments
projects.description: As Project Leader & AI/Computer Vision Engineer, I led the development and experimental evaluation of a computer vision system for automated trash detection in mountain hiking trail environments using YOLOv12. I coordinated the project workflow from dataset preparation and methodology design to model training, evaluation, analysis, and research publication. The project integrated UAVVaste, TACO, and a self-collected dataset from Mount Burangrang, West Java, into a unified trash detection dataset, supported by preprocessing and augmentation techniques designed to improve robustness against illumination variation, occlusion, scale changes, and complex natural backgrounds. I trained and evaluated five YOLOv12 variants (N, S, M, L, and X), comparing their performance using mAP@50, mAP@50:95, and mAP@75, while also analyzing computational complexity, inference speed, FLOPs, and memory consumption against YOLOv8 and Faster R-CNN baselines. The experiments achieved a maximum mAP@50 of 0.7820 with YOLOv12M, while YOLOv12L achieved the highest mAP@75 of 0.4782. The resulting research was published as an IEEE conference paper at the 2026 International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI 2026).

projects.title: AI Research Collaboration & Lecturer Expertise Mapping System for Telkom University
projects.description:
Designed and developed an end-to-end AI-powered platform for mapping research expertise and recommending research collaborations among lecturers at the Faculty of Informatics, Telkom University. The system automatically collects academic profiles, publications, citation metrics, and co-authorship data from multiple sources, then analyzes semantic similarities to identify potential research collaborations through AI-based recommendations.

As the Backend & Data Integration Engineer, I architected and implemented the complete data pipeline, including asynchronous web scraping with Playwright, OpenAlex and SINTA integration, Gemini-powered structured data extraction, PostgreSQL database design, ETL workflows, vector embedding generation using Sentence Transformers, and an AI-based recommendation engine powered by cosine similarity. I also developed the backend APIs and data infrastructure supporting both a Streamlit prototype and a production Laravel dashboard, enabling visualization of lecturer profiles, research statistics, collaboration networks, and AI research expertise across the faculty.

projects.title: Morse Code to Eye Blink Decoder for Assistive Communication Web App
projects.description:
Developed an assistive communication system that translates Morse code generated through eye blinks into natural language text, enabling hands-free communication for individuals with severe speech and motor impairments. This project was completed as part of a Computing Project assignment in collaboration with the Artificial Intelligence Laboratory.

As Project Lead and AI Engineer, I led project planning and development while designing and implementing the AI-based eye blink detection pipeline. The system combines computer vision and deep learning techniques to accurately classify eye states, distinguish short and long blinks, decode Morse code sequences, and generate meaningful text output in real time.

This project explores the application of artificial intelligence and human-computer interaction to improve accessibility and communication, demonstrating how AI-driven assistive technologies can help bridge communication barriers for individuals with disabilities.

projects.title: SehatMOK: Makan Olah Kelola – Smart Nutrition & Food Inventory Platform
projects.description:
SehatMok is a health and nutrition management platform that helps users track daily nutrition, manage food inventory, discover AI-generated recipes from available ingredients, plan meals, monitor hydration, and organize grocery lists. The platform consists of web and mobile applications supported by a centralized backend API.

As a Mobile Developer and AI Engineer, I developed the Flutter mobile application and contributed to the AI-powered recipe recommendation system using Google Gemini. My work included mobile UI implementation, API integration, authentication, offline support, and intelligent recipe generation based on ingredient availability.

projects.title: Chipkost: Kost Management Web Based Application
projects.description:
Chipkost is a boarding house (kost) management application that helps property owners manage rentals, tenants, payments, and financial reports through a centralized digital system. The application is designed to simplify daily operations, reduce manual administration, and improve financial transparency.

In this project, I was responsible for UI/UX design, frontend development, quality assurance, and DevOps. My contributions included designing intuitive user flows and interfaces, implementing responsive frontend features, conducting functional and usability testing, and managing deployment workflows to ensure application stability and reliability. This project strengthened my experience in building end-to-end digital products from design to production.

projects.title: EcoHike: Automatic Trash Monitoring System on Hiking Trail Mobile Application
projects.description:
Led a multidisciplinary team to develop EcoHike, an offline-first mobile system for automatic waste detection on mountain hiking trails using YOLOv12. The solution enables real-time object detection directly on smartphones, designed for hands-free field operation via chest strap and capable of functioning without internet connectivity in remote environments.

As Project Leader, I was responsible for defining the system architecture, coordinating model development and mobile integration, overseeing dataset strategy and evaluation, and ensuring seamless synchronization between offline mobile inference and the backend analytics dashboard. The project evaluates multiple YOLOv12 variants and demonstrates an effective balance between accuracy and efficiency for deployment on resource-constrained devices.

This project aims to support environmental conservation, data-driven trail management, and scalable AI adoption in real-world outdoor settings.

projects.title: AI-Driven Credit Risk Analysis for Microfinance and MSMEs in Indonesia
projects.description:
Led a team in a data mining competition focused on credit risk analysis in Indonesia’s microfinance and MSME (UMKM) sector, aiming to support sustainable digital financing growth. The project leveraged data-driven and AI-based approaches to identify risk patterns related to borrower characteristics, business sectors, collateral types, educational background, and regional factors across multiple provinces.

As Project Leader, I was responsible for defining the analytical strategy, overseeing data preprocessing and feature engineering, guiding model experimentation, and ensuring robust evaluation on imbalanced class distributions using Macro-averaged F1 Score. This metric ensured equal importance across all risk classes, preventing bias toward dominant classes and improving the reliability of credit risk assessment models. The project strengthened my experience in financial data analytics, credit scoring, and applied machine learning for real-world fintech challenges.

projects.title: A Comparative Analysis of YOLOv12 and RF-DETR for Weapon Detection in CCTV Footage
projects.description: This project explores a transformer-based approach to weapon detection using RF-DETR, evaluating its performance on CCTV surveillance footage. Emphasizing accuracy and real-time capability, the study demonstrates RF-DETR’s potential for enhancing public safety through intelligent threat monitoring. The paper is published on an IEEE, 5th ICSINTESA in November 2025.

posts.content:
Grateful to have presented our research at ICoDSA 2026!

It was a great experience participating as an Author at the 9th International Conference on Data Science and its Applications (ICoDSA 2026), held on 21–22 September 2026.

Our paper, “An Eye Blink Morse Code Decoder with Hybrid Vision Models and IndoBERT,” presents an assistive communication system that translates eye blinks into Morse code and converts them into readable Indonesian text. The approach combines MediaPipe FaceMesh and YOLOv26-cls for hybrid eye-state detection, personalized calibration for individual blinking patterns, and IndoBERT for language-aware text refinement.

Huge thanks to my fellow authors Gilbert Lumbantoruan, Muhammad Rifqi Setiawan, Ahmad Taufiq Nur Rohman, and Parman Sukarno for the collaboration and hard work throughout this research.

Special thanks to AI Lab Telkom University, and especially Ahmad Taufiq Nur Rohman and Parman Sukarno, for the guidance, support, and encouragement throughout the research and publication process.

Although I initially didn’t expect to do my internship internally on campus, it turned out to be a valuable experience where I gained practical skills in backend development, data engineering, AI, and research-oriented system development.

Thank you to Dr. Ghaniaviyanto and everyone at the School of Computing and Faculty of Informatics who supported and guided me throughout this journey!

I’m excited to share that our paper “A Comparative Analysis of YOLOv12 and RF-DETR for Weapon Detection in CCTV Footage” has been published on IEEE Xplore by the IEEE.
This work explores the challenge of automated weapon detection in CCTV surveillance, where occlusion, varying viewpoints, and low-resolution imagery often impact detection performance. We compared YOLOv12 variants with the transformer-based RF-DETR model using challenging CCTV footage and evaluated generalization on an unseen camera viewpoint.
The results show that RF-DETR outperforms all YOLOv12 variants, highlighting the stronger robustness of transformer-based architectures for real-world surveillance scenarios.
Special thanks to the team at the AI Laboratory for the collaboration and support throughout this research.
 
Muhammad Syafiq Aqilla
 
Arnoldus Bryan Hendry
 
Muhammad Rafly Arjasubrata
